title: Industry reports label some table facts as format: paragraph, so neither validation lane checks them
description:
Capturing this for later scoping. Definition of done and acceptance criteria are yours to write.

## What is happening

A fact whose `exact_paragraph` is a row of a markdown table is being written into research notes with `format: paragraph`. The validation service routes on that label, so those facts fall between the two lanes:

* the verbatim lane refuses them, correctly, because a table row is not prose authority (verdict `out_of_scope` / `structured_evidence`),
* the visual lane never sees them, because it selects facts by their `format` label and `paragraph` is not in its scope.

Result: nothing validates the number, and the consumer gets an ambiguous verdict rather than a checked one. With `format: table` (or `graph`) plus a `page_no`, the same fact goes to the visual lane and gets checked against the rendered page image, which is the check this evidence actually needs.

## Scale

Measured over the 22-report corpus in the validation repo on 2026-08-03: 849 facts, spread across 17 of the 22 reports. Most common sources: [pib.gov.in](<http://pib.gov.in>) (383 facts), [trade.eepcindia.org](<http://trade.eepcindia.org>) (133), [agriculture.canada.ca](<http://agriculture.canada.ca>) (31), [mnre.gov.in](<http://mnre.gov.in>) (31).

## Examples

From `5_star_hotel_in_jharsuguda__new_17`, section `capital_expenditure_pattern`, all carrying `format: paragraph`:

* `F18`: `|2009-14 |₹ 838 Cr./year | |2025-26 |₹ 10,599 Cr. (Nearly 13 times) |`
  Source is a two-column PIB table headed `|**Period** |**Outlay** |`.
* `F20`: `|2 |Jharsuguda - Sardega New Line (50 Km) |1,598 |`
  One row of the sanctioned-projects table.
* `F22`: `|18 |Jharsuguda-Bilaspur 4 th line (206 Km) |2,596 |`

And a fragment case from the same report, section `competitive_scenario`:

* `F10`: `26. |Odisha |5 |`

## What the validation service needs

Per `docs/INPUT_CONTRACT.md` in the validation-service repo: `format: table` or `graph`, plus `page_no` (a positive integer) when the source is a PDF, since the visual lane renders the cited page.

## Notes

* Forward looking only. No backfill of past runs is being asked for.
* The full per-row list is committed at `evals/analysis/scope_worklist.jsonl` in validation-service; filter `bucket == "table_row_quoted_as_paragraph"` for all 849 rows with report, section, fact id, source URL, and the quote.
* Background and method: `docs/SCOPE_GAPS.md` in the same repo.

title: Data connectors broker architecture - PoC
description:
Validate an architecture that lets the report-generation agent pull context from external data sources (internal document libraries, regulatory/financial APIs, etc.) without editing agent prompts or code each time a new source is added. All connectors sit behind one broker tool exposed to sub-agents; the agent never sees a connector's raw tools directly, so adding a 10th connector costs a registry entry, not a codebase change.

How to verify:

1. Sub-agents request context through one broker tool; connector-specific tools are never registered in the agent's own tool list — confirmed by inspecting the live session's tool registry.
2. Broker correctly routes a natural-language request to the right connector and tool, including for a connector never seen at design time (test with mock connectors and live connectors covering distinct access patterns including both APIs and MCPs).
3. Duplicate/repeated connector calls across parallel sub-agents are served from cache, not re-fetched.
4. OAuth-based connectors (e.g. Google Drive) support user-consented, scope-limited access — access is restricted to an explicitly granted folder/resource, not the user's entire account, and tokens refresh automatically without re-prompting.

title: Deterministic figure verification and highlighting in Download Financials
description:
Gemini reads the PDF and produces the table. This checks its figures against the figures actually printed on the page, flags the ones the page doesn't support, and highlights the row each figure sits on.

Nothing here asks a model. It's string matching over counted occurrences, so when it gets something wrong that's a bug with a fix, not an error rate to live with.

Runs only where [BYN-43](https://linear.app/byndai/issue/BYN-43/native-text-vs-ocrscanned-classification-for-download-financials) says the page's text can be trusted.

## The approach

**Compare printed forms, never parsed numbers.** If you turn both sides into numbers first, `1.234` and `1,234` become the same thing — and that confusion is exactly one of the mistakes we're looking for. So the figures are compared as text.

**Count occurrences, don't just ask "is it there".** If the page prints a value twice and the table holds it five times, three of them are wrong. Asking "does this number appear on the page" passes all five.

**Work out where the table is from the transcription's own figures.** Most of what Gemini extracted is correct, so most of it matches something really printed — and those matches show where on the page the table sits. We never try to detect tables; the answers reveal where they came from. Anything printed outside that area, like page numbers, note references or the schedule below the statement, can't back a figure.

**Pool across the statement's pages.** One statement often runs over two or three pages, and Gemini returns a single table for all of them, so the counting has to span them too.

**When a count disagrees, flag every instance of that figure.** We know some of them are wrong but not which ones. Picking a few would point a reviewer at cells just as likely to be right, and quietly bless the rest.

Row highlighting works off the same page text — each row's printed label is matched to where it appears, which gives the box to draw.

One thing it can't see: a real figure sitting under the wrong column or the wrong row. The counts still balance, so it passes. That's why the output is only ever a flag for a human, never a correction.

title: Native-text vs OCR/scanned classification for Download Financials
description:
Work out whether a statement's pages are the document's own text, or a picture of a document with recognised text laid over it.

This matters because a PDF doesn't store letters. It stores shapes, plus a table saying what each shape means. So the text you pull out of a page can be wrong in ways that don't show on screen at all. And a scanned page with OCR text behind it looks like real text but is a guess about a picture.

Everything downstream compares Gemini's figures against the page. If the page's text is a guess, we'd be checking one guess against another.

## The approach

Before trusting a page, ask a few questions about it:

* Is the page just a picture? A full-page image means it's a scan.
* Is the text drawn invisibly? That's the fingerprint of an OCR layer sitting behind a scan so it stays selectable.
* Do the fonts actually produce readable characters, or garbage?
* Is any text hidden — painted white on white, or covered by something drawn over it afterwards?
* Does the text carry a recogniser's tell-tales? A letter standing in for a digit (`O` for zero, `S` for five), or control characters where something tried to read a rubber stamp or a signature.

The rule running through all of it: **judge what the text actually is, not what the file says about itself.** A file admitting its font has no lookup table doesn't mean the text came out wrong — so look at what came out. Equally, not finding a problem isn't proof there isn't one, if we couldn't have seen it in the first place.

If any page of a statement fails, that whole statement is dropped. A scanned filing produces nothing rather than something we can't stand behind.

title: One-Pager Generation for Delivered News
description:
**Goal -** Allow users to select delivered news items from the frontend and generate a standardised, high-quality PDF One-Pager

**Context**

* **User Flow:** The user selects target news items on the frontend and triggers One-Pager generation.
* **Backend Architecture:** The request hits the `@one-pager` service, which executes an AI skill against the LLM/model using a fixed HTML template.
* **Deliverable:** The model fills the HTML template with summarized/generated content, converts it, and returns a PDF downloadable on the frontend.

### **How to Verify**

* **UI & Visual Validation:**
  * Confirm the rendered One-Pager layout and design are visual- and format-correct from the UI/PDF output perspective for **Default users and Prop Equity**.
* **Data Quality & Accuracy:**
  * Verify that the AI skill accurately parses, summarizes, and maps news content into the designated template sections without hallucination or truncation.
* **End-to-End Reliability Test:**
  * Perform successful end-to-end generation tests using **at least 50 news items** containing full news payloads to ensure pipeline stability and output consistency.
